evidence.summaryExcerpt: Standing, not lying down: Several sources agree on this. The Sistine Chapel ceiling article says Vasari and Condivi reported that he worked standing, and that another biographer, Paolo Giovio, had imagined otherwise. According to Vasari and Condivi, Michelangelo painted in a standing position, not lying on his back, as another biographer, Paolo Giovio, imagined. Britannica's explainer describes him standing on an extensive scaffold, reaching up and craning his neck.
